question: Should this Gateway public-network hardening land as default-on core behavior, or should the rate limit, HSTS, audit log, IP ACL, and bind-fallback changes be split and/or made explicit opt-in config?
rationale: The diff changes security defaults, persistence/privacy behavior, config contract, and availability semantics for existing Gateway deployments, which requires maintainer intent beyond mechanical code repair.

options.title: Require opt-in or split controls
options.body: Make each control schema-backed and documented, keep compatibility-preserving defaults unless maintainers explicitly approve a stricter default, and require real Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Accept stricter defaults
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally own default-on throttling, HSTS, audit logging, and fail-closed bind behavior if the PR documents upgrade impact and proves the real paths.

options.title: Pause this bundle
options.body: Close or pause the broad branch and ask for smaller PRs that each solve one hardening surface with focused policy review and proof.

recommendation.title: Require opt-in or split controls
recommendation.body: Make each control schema-backed and documented, keep compatibility-preserving defaults unless maintainers explicitly approve a stricter default, and require real Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway/config/security commits and net-policy extraction make this the best available owner for default/security-boundary direction.
